description: SPEI is a Python package for calculating and plotting drought indices from user-provided time series. It uses Pandas, SciPy and Matplotlib to handle the input series, fit index calculations and display changes over time. Its geographic coverage, sampling interval and historical period are properties of the input precipitation, evapotranspiration or other water-balance data; the software does not publish a drought map. The own repository and package instructions are public under MIT. The resulting indices can help define drought scenarios or compare conditions used in reservoir, supply and land-water simulations. A caveat is that a drought index depends on the chosen accumulation period, reference distribution and input quality, and it is not a direct measurement of water-system failure. The catalogue data-spei-hr-global-high-resolution-drought-indices record is a separate published index dataset, not this computation package. No first-review software draft or catalogue software record matched SPEI. This review read the JOSS description and repository documentation without calculating an index.
